entry.title: BIP 110: update status to closed
entry.summary:
In the email from Sjors, a detailed explanation is provided on the process and implications of closing a Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP). He clarifies that closing a BIP does not result in the confiscation of coins nor does it prevent anyone from running nodes or continuing mining activities. However, he notes that catching up after such actions would be highly unlikely due to the competitive disadvantage created by the timing.
Sjors also discusses the technical feasibility of operating under an outdated BIP, using BIP 12 as an example. He describes a hypothetical scenario where he could initiate a node based on BIP 12 and start mining blocks by forking at the activation height of P2SH (Pay to Script Hash), effectively ignoring newer protocol updates. Despite the ability to mine blocks under such conditions, he points out that such blocks would not be rejected by modern Bitcoin Core software since it no longer uses checkpoints. Nonetheless, this approach would not allow him to catch up with the current blockchain tip, rendering the effort futile.
Additionally, he expresses his perspective on BIP 110, noting that the ineffectiveness of this proposal as both a policy and a consensus rule was apparent to him years ago. He acknowledges that realization might come slower to others, and some may never see it as unfeasible.
Sjors seeks input on criteria for reasonably closing a BIP, suggesting that now might be an appropriate time to consider closure but showing openness to other opinions. This discussion highlights the complexities involved in managing and evolving blockchain protocols through BIPs, illustrating the careful considerations required to maintain network integrity and forward compatibility.
